spec.title: 30 seconds of continuous frame supply to the worker
spec.input: an open camera; the scheduler driven by requestVideoFrameCallback; no load injected
spec.expected: frames reach the worker and results return continuously for at least 30 000 ms
spec.passCriteria: the longest unstressed contiguous segment is >= 30000 ms; mean delivered rate within it >= 15 fps; longest gap between results <= 2000 ms; lost frames <= 2% of admitted; the page was never hidden during the segment
spec.failureCondition: any of the above unmet. Never starting the pipeline is PENDING, not FAIL

testResults.observed: 36.1 s unstressed, 720 frames at 19.92 fps, longest gap 122.5 ms, 0/1705 lost, 6 paced out, 88 backpressured
testResults.reason: frames were supplied to the worker continuously for the full window with no stall beyond tolerance; frames declined by pacing and backpressure are the scheduler working, and are counted separately from losses

spec.title: Worker processing, on real camera pixels
spec.input: the acquisition route selected by the runtime probe; the preprocessing worker; the 1 Hz provenance cross-check
spec.expected: preprocessing runs off the UI thread, on pixels that came from the camera, producing a self-consistent grayscale pyramid
spec.passCriteria: worker scope has no document and a real WorkerGlobalScope; >= 90% of measured per-frame processing time is spent in the worker; >= 5 cross-checks over a scene whose own luma varied by at least 3 standard deviations, with median mean-luma disagreement <= 10/255 and <= 0.5 of that spread; 3 levels, each byte length equal to its width x height and each the halving of the level above
spec.failureCondition: any of the four unmet. A cross-check median above tolerance fails outright: it means the worker image is not the camera image

testResults.observed: route VIDEO_FRAME, 99.3% of processing time in the worker (18.84 ms vs 0.13 ms UI); 87 cross-checks over a scene varying by 3.856, median Δluma 0.083 / max 0.146; strip Δ peak 11.996; levels 640x480 / 320x240 / 160x120
testResults.reason: preprocessing ran in a scope with no document, took the overwhelming majority of per-frame processing time, produced a pyramid whose geometry checks out, and produced an image that agrees with an independent measurement of the same video frame — which a fabricated or stale image could not do

spec.title: Resolution fallback
spec.input: measured worker latency rising until the controller steps down the tier ladder
spec.expected: the processing resolution really changes, and every frame respects its tier
spec.passCriteria: two or more distinct processing resolutions produced, read from buffers the worker returned; at least one recorded downward step with the latency that caused it; no frame above its tier pixel budget or above 1280x720; aspect ratio preserved to within 2% and never upscaled
spec.failureCondition: the tier changed but the produced buffers did not; any frame above its budget; an aspect-ratio break; any upscale

testResults.observed: resolutions produced: 1280x720 -> 640x480 -> 960x540 -> 480x360; 4 downward step(s), deepest REDUCED 640x360@20; 0 over budget, 0 upscaled, worst aspect error 0%
testResults.reason: the processing resolution really changed and every frame stayed within its tier's budget, preserved its source aspect ratio and was never upscaled. at least one downward step was taken with no load injected — the device could not hold its tier on its own, which is worth knowing

spec.title: FPS adaptation
spec.input: the same measured latency stream; the controller target-rate ladder
spec.expected: the target rate adapts to measured load, never below the §10 floor, with a measurable effect
spec.passCriteria: the target rate changed at least once and every selected target is >= 15 fps; each change carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against; after the last downward step that lowered the processing resolution, the following window's median worker latency is lower than the window that triggered it; once load was removed the pipeline returned to >= 15 fps and the controller recovered at least one step
spec.failureCondition: a selected target below 15 fps; a change with no measurement behind it; no recovery after load was removed; more than 4 changes in any 10 s window

testResults.observed: 2 rate change(s) among 9 ladder move(s); now HIGH 1280x720@30 delivering 20 fps; the last resolution step took median worker latency 63.9 ms -> 38.5 ms; 3 recovery step(s)
testResults.reason: the target rate moved because measured latency moved, never below the 15 fps floor; the downward step measurably reduced worker latency, and the controller climbed back once the load was gone

spec.title: UI-thread budget
spec.input: the synchronous cost of the pipeline own work on the callbacks where a frame is admitted
spec.expected: the UI thread keeps a 60 Hz budget while the pipeline runs
spec.passCriteria: mean and 95th percentile pipeline UI cost <= 16.7 ms over >= 100 admitted frames, excluding the 1 Hz provenance cross-check whose own cost is reported in full
spec.failureCondition: either statistic over budget. Advisory: §34 ranks correctness above performance

testResults.observed: UI 0.13 ms mean / 0.3 ms p95 / 2.4 ms max over 1705 frames via VIDEO_FRAME; the worker took 18.84 ms mean; the 1 Hz cross-check cost 3.3 ms mean
testResults.reason: the UI thread kept its 60 Hz budget while the worker carried the per-frame cost, which is the division §10 asks for and the one §H.1 said a main-thread readback could not deliver

spec.title: Source geometry is per-frame
spec.input: the device rotated while the pipeline runs, changing the source frame size
spec.expected: the processing size is re-derived from the new source geometry, and every frame record carries its own
spec.passCriteria: at least two distinct source sizes observed; the first completed frame after the change carries a processing size derived from the new source geometry; every completed frame record carries its own source and processing size
spec.failureCondition: the processing size stays derived from a stale source size, or frame records share one session-wide geometry

testResults.observed: source sizes 1280x720 -> 640x480; processing sizes 960x540 -> 1280x720 -> 640x480 -> 480x360; 1025 frame(s) since the last change
testResults.reason: the source geometry is read per frame and the processing size re-derived from it, so a rotation mid-scan is carried through rather than smoothed over (§H.0)

controller.note: Every decision carries the median worker latency and the budget it was compared against. The controller reads no clock of its own — only the timestamps on the samples it is given (§59).

segmentLog.note: The timeline is cut wherever load injection was switched on or off. FRAME-001 reads the longest unstressed segment; stressed segments are measured and reported but never counted toward continuity.

crossCheckDetail.note: Each pair is one video frame measured twice: on the main thread with an independent 64x48 readback, and in the worker on the pixels the pipeline actually delivered. The readback costs what §H.1 measured, which is why it runs at 1 Hz and is excluded from the pipeline UI cost in FRAME-005.

pipeline.note: Frames declined by rate pacing (pacedOut) are the scheduler working as designed and are not drops. Frames declined because the worker was busy (backpressured) are deliberate too. Only `lost` counts frames that were handed over and never came back, and only that is held against FRAME-001.
